policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere הימני and ketiv הימיני are orthographic variants of the same adjective 'right (side)', differing only in the plene yod. ASV 'thou shalt lie on thy right side' renders that sense and cannot distinguish the spellings; no ASV note is mapped to this unit. Both readings remain compatible and the qere base fallback carries the projection.

Qere צפיעי and ketiv צפועי differ only in the vowel letter (yod vs waw) of the same construct noun for cattle dung. ASV 'cow’s dung' renders that sense under either spelling, and no ASV note is mapped to this unit. Both readings remain compatible and the qere base fallback carries the projection.
